newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann cuts D2 mobile phone charges.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann cuts D2 mobile phone charges.

text.p: Germany's Mannesmann AG, following a lead set by Deutsche Telekom AG, said on Wednesday it would cut rental rates and call charges for users of its Mannesmann Mobilfunk unit's D2 mobile phone network.
Mannesmann said in a statement it would halve the monthly fee on a mobile phone to 24.95 marks, while the cost of a one-minute conversation would fall to 99 pfennigs.
The price cuts would take effect from October 30. Minimum contract duration would be two years, Mannesmann said.
"With these new rates, Mannesmann Mobilfunk is developing its existing price structure. The goal is to win new customers with targeted offers," the statement said.

Mannesmann appears to have undercut price cuts announced last week by Deutsche Telekom, which stunned its competitors by slashing its monthly fee to 29 marks from 49 marks. A news conference was to be held later to detail the price reductions.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk is owned by Mannesmann and AirTouch Communications of the United States. The D2 network had been winning around 80,000 customers a month, undercutting the market share of Telekom's D1 system.
